learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how to pair elements between sets using Cartesian Products, establish 'Relations' between them, and master 'Functions' as strictly ruled mathematical machines!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: If you have Set A and Set B, their Cartesian Product ($A \times B$) is the set of all possible ordered pairs $(a, b)$ where 'a' comes from A and 'b' comes from B. Think of it as mixing and matching every shirt you own with every pair of pants.

A Relation is simply a subset of the Cartesian Product $A \times B$. It links elements from Set A to Set B based on a specific rule (e.g., 'a is the square of b'). The set of all valid inputs is the Domain, and the set of actual outputs is the Range.

A Function is a very strict relation where EVERY element in Set A has ONE and ONLY ONE output in Set B. Imagine a vending machine: if you press the button for Cola (input), you should get exactly one Cola (output). You can't get two different drinks from one button press!

Functions can be added, subtracted, multiplied, and divided just like numbers. You will also learn to plot graphs for standard real functions like the Identity function, Constant function, Polynomials, Modulus function, and Signum function.

fun_activity.title: ⚙️ The Function Machine Game
fun_activity.instructions: Draw a box and call it 'Machine f(x) = 2x + 1'. Feed different numbers (Domain) into the top of the machine. If you drop in a 3, the machine doubles it and adds 1, popping out a 7 (Range). Try feeding it -5, 0, and 10 to see what the machine generates!

exam_tips: 📌 All functions are relations, but not all relations are functions! A relation fails to be a function if a single input has multiple outputs.
📌 When finding the Domain of a function like $f(x) = \frac{1}{x-2}$, set the denominator to not equal zero ($x \neq 2$). The domain is all Real numbers except 2: $\mathbb{R} - \{2\}$.
📌 Be prepared to draw the graph of the Modulus function $f(x) = |x|$ (V-shape) and the Signum function; they are examiner favorites.
quick_recap: ⭐ The number of elements in $A \times B$ is $n(A) \times n(B)$.
⭐ The Codomain is the entire Set B, while the Range is only the specific elements in Set B that actually got mapped.
⭐ A function cannot have one input mapping to two different outputs (vertical line test on a graph).
